probes.name: Same state and seed reproduce transitions
No inventory during supply delay means no purchases
No spending balance means no purchases
Return shock changes returns without changing initial same-day sales
Immature and future rewards cannot affect fitted coefficients
Plans use past cutoffs and fixed publication times

goals.label: Additional modeled PayPal value
goals.rule: 95% lower bound above $0 per 100 shoppers over 70 campaign days

goals.label: Value beyond matched rules
goals.rule: 95% lower bound above $0 versus rules with the same local learner

goals.label: Merchant economics
goals.rule: 95% lower bound no worse than −$0 aggregate merchant contribution

goals.label: Worst-case loss
goals.rule: Worst observed case no worse than −$50; not a guarantee about unseen cases

goals.label: Accounting, maturity and authority
goals.rule: Zero accounting, eligibility, inventory, maturity or virtual budget violations

goals.label: Autonomous multi-agent advantage
goals.rule: Needs fresh agent and single-planner trials on unseen evidence with matched tools and budgets

goals.label: Real-world validity
goals.rule: Needs observed behavioral calibration; catalog and sandbox receipts alone are insufficient

audit.costBasis: Provider token estimate, not a billing invoice

semanticReview.method: Manual, non-exhaustive source-trace annotations. Structural validity is not factual correctness.

findings.finding: Trend described as a decline despite 119 recent purchases versus 111 previous purchases.
Reward-prediction MSE used as support for a policy; prediction error does not establish incremental campaign value.
Claimed organic had the highest merchant contribution; the rules branch was higher.
Claimed strategy changes prevented stabilization without a causal ablation.

audit.scope: One recorded live run. No new agent calls during the benchmark.

costs.basis: Every saved-plan world is charged the full source-run token estimate, including rejected attempts and final review. This is an allocation sensitivity, not a new bill. Rules use no model API. Local CPU seconds are measured; electricity/hardware/labor are unpriced, not assumed free.

limitations: Plans and their observed publication delays are replayed; Gemini does not inspect new test evidence. Local coefficients are freshly fitted.
Intervals reflect seed variation under five fixed behavioral scenarios; they do not cover model misspecification, fresh LLM variability or production customers.
All cumulative curves use fully matured sale cohorts, reconstructed after day114; they are not information available to agents on that day.
Local compute time is measured but not priced; API estimates are not billing invoices.
Full source model cost is allocated to each saved-plan world; no new API cost was incurred.
No single-planner comparator has been run; this cannot establish the value of agent count.
No seed-specific tuning. Once viewed these evaluation seeds are regression cases, not reusable untouched holdouts.

cohortDiagnostic.interpretation: Every baseline lapsed shopper returned within 70 days without outreach. This horizon has a ceiling effect; zero reactivation lift does not validate a realistic churn model.

figures.name: economic-impact
figures.caption: Paired mean and 95% uncertainty by scenario. A positive mean alone does not pass the economic goal.

figures.name: cumulative-value
figures.caption: Cumulative economic effect with pointwise uncertainty. Negative regions remain visible.

figures.name: merchant-and-reactivation
figures.caption: Merchant economics and incremental reactivation of a cohort fixed before campaign activation.

figures.name: agent-reliability
figures.caption: Original live-agent evidence. Factual mistakes are annotated separately from structural guard tests.

figures.name: version-progress
figures.caption: One measured version, with uncertainty. The chart does not imply an improvement that has not been tested.
